## iNaturalist data

The data were downloaded from <https://www.naturalista.uy/observations/export> using the following parameters
`quality_grade=any&identifications=any&place_id=12416&verifiable=true`.  

```{r}
#| label: inat-data
#| warning: false
#| message: false

inat_mdeo <- read_csv('data/observations-536732.csv')
```

### Quick summary

::: {.callout-note appearance='simple'}
Some of the code used here is from:

Grattarola, F. (2024). reportiNat: Creación de reportes de proyectos de iNaturalist usando quarto [Code]. <https://github.com/bienflorencia/LatinR2024>
:::

```{r}
#| label: inat-data-summary
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| code-fold: true

inat_mdeo %>% 
  summarise(n_records = n(),
            n_users = n_distinct(user_id),
            n_taxa = n_distinct(scientific_name),
            n_species = n_distinct(taxon_species_name, na.rm = T)) %>% 
  kableExtra::kbl(
    col.names = c('Number of records',
                  'Number of users',
                  'Number of taxa',
                  'Number of species'),
    format.args = list(decimal.mark = '.',
                       big.mark = ','),
    digits=2,
                  booktabs = T) %>% 
  kableExtra::kable_styling(latex_options = c('striped', 'hold_position'))
```

#### Temporal coverage

```{r}
#| label: temporal-summary
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| code-fold: true


detectPeriod <- function(datos, timecol){
  
  period_timecol <- datos %>% 
    mutate(timecol=as_datetime(eval(parse(text = timecol)))) %>% 
    summarise(start=min(timecol, na.rm=T),
              end=max(timecol, na.rm=T),
              hours_active=time_length(interval(start, end), 'hours'),
              days_active=time_length(interval(start, end), 'days'),
              years_active=time_length(interval(start, end), 'years'))
  
  if(period_timecol$days_active<=2){
    periodVariables <- tibble(timecol = timecol,
                              count_variable = 'records_per_hour',
                              unit_variable = '1 hour',
                              unit_text = 'hora')
  } else if(period_timecol$days_active>2 &
            period_timecol$days_active<=4){
    periodVariables <- tibble(timecol = timecol,
                              count_variable = 'records_per_hour',
                              unit_variable = '6 hours',
                              unit_text = '6 horas')
  } else if(period_timecol$days_active>4 &
            period_timecol$days_active<=7){
    periodVariables <- tibble(timecol = timecol,
                              count_variable = 'records_per_day',
                              unit_variable = '1 day',
                              unit_text = 'día')
  }else if(period_timecol$days_active>7 &
            period_timecol$days_active<=365){
    periodVariables <- tibble(timecol = timecol,
                              count_variable = 'records_per_week',
                              unit_variable = '1 week',
                              unit_text = 'semana')
  } else if(period_timecol$days_active>365 &
            period_timecol$days_active<=730){
    periodVariables <- tibble(timecol = timecol,
                              count_variable = 'records_per_month',
                              unit_variable = '1 month',
                              unit_text = 'mes')
  } 
  else{
    periodVariables <- tibble(timecol = timecol,
                              count_variable = 'records_per_year',
                              unit_variable = '1 year',
                              unit_text = '1 año')
  }
  return(periodVariables)
}

periodVars <- detectPeriod(inat_mdeo,
                           timecol = 'observed_on')

temporal_df <- inat_mdeo %>% 
           mutate(time_observed_at=as_datetime(observed_on)) %>%
           mutate(metric=case_when(
             periodVars$count_variable=='records_per_hour' ~ 
               hour(time_observed_at),
             periodVars$count_variable=='records_per_day' ~ 
               day(time_observed_at),
             periodVars$count_variable=='records_per_week' ~ 
               week(time_observed_at),
             periodVars$count_variable=='records_per_month' ~ 
               month(time_observed_at),
             periodVars$count_variable=='records_per_year' ~ 
               year(time_observed_at))) %>% 
           add_count(iconic_taxon_name, 
                     metric,
                     name=periodVars$count_variable) %>%
           mutate(time_observed_at=ceiling_date(observed_on,
                                                unit=periodVars$unit_variable)) %>%
           distinct(time_observed_at, .keep_all = T) %>% 
           mutate(label = paste0(
             # 'Fecha y hora de observación: ', time_observed_at, 
             'Registros cada ', periodVars$unit_text, 
             ':', 
             eval(parse(text = periodVars$count_variable))))

ggplotly(ggplot(temporal_df, aes(x=observed_on, 
                         y=eval(parse(text = periodVars$count_variable)), 
                         group=2, text=label)) +
           geom_line(color='red', linewidth = 1.5)+
           geom_point(col="grey10", size=0.5) +
           scale_x_datetime(breaks = periodVars$unit_variable,
                            date_labels="%d\n%H:%M") +
           theme_light()+
           labs(x='', y= 'Número de observaciones') , 
         tooltip="text", 
         dynamicTicks = T) 
```

inat_mdeo %>% 
  group_by(user_login) %>% 
  summarise(observations=n(),

            species=n_distinct(taxon_species_name)) %>% 
  arrange(desc(observations)) %>% 
  mutate(observations_q = case_when(observations <= 1 ~ '1',
                                    observations <= 10 ~ '<10',
                                    observations > 10 & observations <= 100 ~ '10 - 100',
                                    observations > 100 & observations <= 500 ~ '100 - 500',
                                    observations > 500 ~ '>500',
                                    .default = NA)) %>%

  scale_fill_brewer(palette = 'Set1', direction = 1) +

### Data cleaning

```{r}
#| label: inat-data-cleaning
#| warning: false
#| message: false

inat_mdeo <- inat_mdeo %>% 
  # filter records with low positional accuracy
  filter(positional_accuracy <= 500) %>% 
  # filter records with obscured coordinates
  filter(coordinates_obscured == F)

# make the data spatial points
inat_mdeo_sf <- st_as_sf(inat_mdeo,
                         coords = c("longitude",
                                    "latitude"),
                         crs = 4326)

# join the grid to the points and count records and species
mvd_inat <- st_join(mvd_grid, inat_mdeo_sf) %>% 
  group_by(id_hex) %>%
  summarise(N = sum(!is.na(taxon_species_name)),
    S = n_distinct(taxon_species_name, na.rm = TRUE)) 
```

## Socio-ecological variables

These variables are proxies for the "participation" and "sampling" filters proposed by [Carlen et al. (2024)](https://doi.org/10.1002/pan3.10592).

| Filter by Carlen et al. (2024) | Variable                                                                 | Denomination          | Expectation                                                                  | Temporal resolution | Source                                                        |
|--------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| Sampling                       | Median Normalized Difference Vegetation Index                            | NDVI                  | Greener areas will have more observations                                    | 2017-2023           | Sentinel-2 (Huang et al., 2021)                               |
| Sampling                       | Median Normalized Difference Moisture Index (NDMI)                       | NDMI                  | Areas with healthier vegetation will have more observations                  | 2017-2023           | Sentinel-2 (Wang and Qu, 2007)                                |
| Sampling                       | Median proportion of built-up area in each cell                          | pNDBI                 | Built-up areas will have less observations                                   | 2017-2023           | Sentinel-2 (Zha et al., 2003)                                 |
| Sampling                       | Proportion of area covered by protected areas                            | protection            | Areas with higher proportions of protected areas will have more observations | 2023                | Uruguayan System of Protected Areas (SNAP)                    |
| Sampling                       | Most frequent Local Climate Zone                                         | LCZ                   | Less dense urban covers will host more observations                          | 2018                | Demuzere et al., (2022)                                       |
| Participation                  | Number of inhabitants                                                    | population            | More people will record more observations                                    | 2011                | Uruguayan National Statistics Institute (INE, 2011)           |
| Participation                  | Number of households                                                     | houses                | Larger number of houses will generate more observations                      | 2011                | Uruguayan National Statistics Institute (INE, 2011)           |
| Participation                  | Average years of formal education among individuals older than 21 years  | education             | Areas with higher levels of education will get more observations             | 2011                | Uruguayan National Statistics Institute (INE, 2011)           |
| Participation                  | Median artificial light at night, measured as radiance (nW cm⁻² sr⁻¹)    | ALAN                  | Well lit areas (more urbanized) will show less observations                  | 2017-2022           | NOAA/VIIRS/DNB (Elvidge et al., 2021)                         |
| Participation                  | Distance to the coastline (in meters)                                    | distance to the coast | Observations will decline along distance from coast due to cultural links    | -                   | Open Street Map Coastline (https://osmcode.org/osmcoastline/) |

## Models

### Merge data

Merge the iNaturalist data with the socio-ecological variables

```{r}
#| label: merge-data
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| code-fold: true

mvd_hex <- st_join(st_join(mvd_env, 
                           mvd_social %>% select(-id_hex), 
                           join = st_equals), 
                   mvd_inat %>% select(-id_hex), 
                   join = st_equals) %>% 
  mutate(pres = ifelse(N>0, 1, 0),
         lcz = as.factor(lcz)) %>% 
  relocate('pres', .after = 'S')
```

### GAM observation occurrence

```{r}
#| label: gam-bin
#| warning: false
#| message: false

fit_bin1 <- gam(pres ~ s(ndvi) + s(ndmi) + 
                 s(pndbi) + lcz + 
                 s(alan) + s(dist_coast) +
                 s(protection) + s(pop) + 
                 s(houses) + s(education),
               family = binomial, data = mvd_hex)

summary(fit_bin1)

# remove: lcz
fit_bin2 <- gam(pres ~ s(ndvi) + s(ndmi)+ 
                  s(pndbi) + s(alan) +
                  s(dist_coast) +s(protection) +s(pop) +
                 s(houses) +s(education), 
                family = binomial, data = mvd_hex)

summary(fit_bin2)

# remove: -pnbi -lcz
fit_bin3 <- gam(pres ~ s(ndvi) + s(ndmi)+ 
                  s(alan) +s(dist_coast) +
                  s(protection) +s(pop) +
                  s(houses) +s(education), 
                family = binomial, data = mvd_hex)


summary(fit_bin3)

# remove: -ndmi -pnbi -lcz 
fit_bin4 <- gam(pres ~ s(ndvi) + s(alan) +
                  s(dist_coast) +s(protection) +s(pop) +
                  s(houses) +s(education), 
                family = binomial, data = mvd_hex)

summary(fit_bin4)

#remove: -pop -ndmi -pnbi -lcz 
fit_bin5 <- gam(pres ~ s(ndvi) + s(alan) +
                  s(dist_coast) +s(protection)+
                  s(houses) + s(education), 
                family = binomial, data = mvd_hex)

summary(fit_bin5)

#remove: -houses -pop -ndmi -pnbi -lcz 
fit_bin6 <- gam(pres ~ s(ndvi) + s(alan) +
                  s(dist_coast) +s(protection)+
                  +s(education), 
                family = binomial, data = mvd_hex)

summary(fit_bin6)
```

#### Model summary results

```{r}
#| label: model-summary-results-bin
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| code-fold: true

output_bin <- cbind(AIC(fit_bin1, fit_bin2, fit_bin3, fit_bin4, 
                    fit_bin5, fit_bin6, k=3.18),
                rsq=c(rsq::rsq(fit_bin1), rsq::rsq(fit_bin2),
                      rsq::rsq(fit_bin3), rsq::rsq(fit_bin4), 
                      rsq::rsq(fit_bin5), rsq::rsq(fit_bin6)),
      formula= as.character(c(formula(fit_bin1), formula(fit_bin2),
                              formula(fit_bin3), formula(fit_bin4),
                              formula(fit_bin5), formula(fit_bin6)))) %>% 
  arrange(AIC)

output_bin %>% knitr::kable()
```

The selected model is `fit_bin6`.

#### Concurvity

```{r}
#| label: concurvity-bin
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| code-fold: true


# Drop geometry and enforce numeric
vars <- c("ndvi", "alan", "dist_coast", "protection", "education")
df_vars <- mvd_hex %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(vars), as.numeric))


# OBSERVATION OCCURRENCE
   
# 1. Concurvity
conc <- concurvity(fit_bin6, full = FALSE)
conc_est <- as.data.frame(conc$estimate)

conc_df <- conc_est %>%
  mutate(term1 = rownames(.)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -term1,
               names_to = "term2",
               values_to = "concurvity")

# 2. Correlation
cor_mat <- cor(df_vars[, vars], use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

cor_df <- as.data.frame(cor_mat) %>%
  mutate(term1 = rownames(.)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -term1,
               names_to = "term2",
               values_to = "correlation")

conc_df$term1<- gsub("^s\\((.*?)\\)$", "\\1", (conc_df$term1))
conc_df$term2<- gsub("^s\\((.*?)\\)$", "\\1", (conc_df$term2))

# 3. Merge concurvity + correlation
plot_df <- left_join(conc_df, cor_df, by = c("term1", "term2")) %>% 
  filter(term1 != 'para' & term2 != 'para')

# 4. Plot
ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = term1, y = term2, fill = concurvity)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(correlation, 2)), size = 3) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "red",
                      limits = c(0, 1),
                      name = "Concurvity (0–1)") +
  coord_equal() +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Observation occurrence",
       subtitle = "Heatmap = concurvity; Numbers = correlations",
       x = "", y = "")

```

#### Plots

```{r}
#| label: model-plots-count
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| code-fold: true

gam.check(fit_count5)
draw(fit_count5)

# Create a plot for lcz
vc <- vcov(fit_count5)

# Get all parameter names
param_names <- colnames(vc)

# Identify LCZ-related terms
lcz_terms <- grep("^lcz", param_names, value = TRUE)

# Extract estimates directly from vcov row names
estimates <- fit_count5$coefficients[lcz_terms]

# Get standard errors
ses <- sqrt(diag(vc[lcz_terms, lcz_terms]))

# Assemble dataframe
plot_df <- data.frame(
  level = gsub("^lcz", "", lcz_terms),
  estimate = estimates,
  se = ses,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# Add 95% confidence intervals
plot_df$lower <- plot_df$estimate - 1.96 * plot_df$se
plot_df$upper <- plot_df$estimate + 1.96 * plot_df$se

# Add reference level manually (effect = 0)
ref_level <- levels(fit_count5$model$lcz)[1]
plot_df <- rbind(
  data.frame(
    level = ref_level,
    estimate = 0,
    se = NA,
    lower = 0,
    upper = 0
  ),
  plot_df
)

# Re-order LCZ levels
plot_df$level <- factor(plot_df$level, levels = sort(as.numeric(unique(plot_df$level))))

# Plot
ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = level, y = estimate)) +
  geom_point(size=6) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), width = 0.2) +
  labs(
    x = "LCZ Category",
    y = "Effect"
  ) +
  theme_classic()
```


#### Concurvity

```{r}
#| label: concurvity-count
#| warning: false
#| message: false
#| code-fold: true


# Drop geometry and enforce numeric
vars <- c("ndmi", "houses", "dist_coast", "protection", "education")
df_vars <- mvd_hex %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(vars), as.numeric))
  
# 1. Concurvity
conc <- concurvity(fit_count5, full = FALSE)
conc_est <- as.data.frame(conc$estimate)

conc_df <- conc_est %>%
  mutate(term1 = rownames(.)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -term1,
               names_to = "term2",
               values_to = "concurvity")

# 2. Correlation
cor_mat <- cor(df_vars[, vars], use = "pairwise.complete.obs")

cor_df <- as.data.frame(cor_mat) %>%
  mutate(term1 = rownames(.)) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = -term1,
               names_to = "term2",
               values_to = "correlation")

conc_df$term1<- gsub("^s\\((.*?)\\)$", "\\1", (conc_df$term1))
conc_df$term2<- gsub("^s\\((.*?)\\)$", "\\1", (conc_df$term2))

# 3. Merge concurvity + correlation
plot_df <- left_join(conc_df, cor_df, by = c("term1", "term2")) %>% 
  filter(term1 != 'para' & term2 != 'para')

# 4. Plot
ggplot(plot_df, aes(x = term1, y = term2, fill = concurvity)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(correlation, 2)), size = 3) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "white", high = "red",
                      limits = c(0, 1),
                      name = "Concurvity (0–1)") +
  coord_equal() +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) +
  labs(title = "Observation count",
       subtitle = "Heatmap = concurvity; Numbers = correlations",
       x = "", y = "")
```
